projects.title: Portfolio accounting audit
projects.question: Can every euro of the published portfolio be reconciled?
projects.method: Replay all 217 signed instrument transactions against frozen EUR-adjusted prices. Recompute fees and cash, reconcile every historical NAV, convert index units to closing share equivalents and independently value the current book. Verify evidence dates and exclude pending instructions.
projects.decision: A risk or performance claim is unusable until cash, positions and P&L agree. The audit supplies the common accounting base for all other projects.
projects.falsifier: Any unexplained NAV difference, future-dated source, stale quote or unprocessed corporate action blocks publication.
projects.next: Extend the forward ledger to explicit ex-date entitlements, payment dates, tax and interest when those events actually occur.
projects.interview: Explain adjusted index units versus real shares, why price plus dividends must not be counted twice, and why an order is not a fill.
projects.finding: All 515 historical NAV marks reconcile. Replayed NAV: €126,505.91; current marks: €127,555.12. Pending order excluded.

projects.title: Capital weights versus risk contributions
projects.question: Which positions consume the portfolio's risk budget?
projects.method: Apply current weights to EUR returns from 2021–2024. Use sample covariance as the transparent baseline and compare 0%, 25%, 50% and 100% shrinkage to constant-correlation and diagonal targets. Compute Euler variance shares, daily historical VaR/ES and a circular block-bootstrap volatility interval. Compare with a recent window.
projects.decision: Small crypto or single-stock capital weights can consume disproportionate risk. Overlapping equity funds require a covariance view rather than a count of holdings.
projects.falsifier: If risk rankings change substantially across windows or shrinkage assumptions, precise risk budgets deserve less confidence; no single covariance matrix is treated as truth.
projects.next: Add verified fund look-through and stress correlations. Estimate shrinkage intensity before using this as an optimiser.
projects.interview: Explain why an empirical ES based on 19 tail observations is fragile and why current weights on past returns are a scenario, not a historical live forecast.
projects.finding: Current weights on the pre-inception sample imply 13.19% annual volatility; daily 97.5% ES is 2.17%. The block-bootstrap volatility range is 11.87%–14.67%.

projects.title: Price and currency attribution
projects.question: Did the first forward week's profit come from assets or currency?
projects.method: Hold share quantities fixed from 18 to 25 September 2026. Decompose EUR P&L exactly into local-price change translated at opening FX and currency change applied to the closing local value. Assign the interaction explicitly to FX.
projects.decision: Unhedged US Treasury and commodity ETF marks can move in EUR even when local prices barely move. Attribute the result before judging the thesis.
projects.falsifier: A change in units, distribution entitlement or other cash flow invalidates this two-endpoint fixed-position calculation and requires a daily ledger.
projects.next: Extend to daily transaction-aware attribution and an explicit, costed currency-hedging counterfactual.
projects.interview: Derive the price/FX cross term. Explain why a USD-listed global equity ETF does not represent pure economic USD exposure.
projects.finding: 18–25 September: €52.27 local-price P&L plus €996.95 currency P&L equals €1,049.21.

projects.title: Duration, convexity and curve risk
projects.question: What does the proposed IEF-to-SHY shift actually change?
projects.method: Price synthetic 2- and 8-year semiannual coupon bonds exactly. Compare duration-convexity approximations, node shocks and non-parallel curve scenarios. Then evaluate a 2%-of-NAV shift using explicitly assumed ETF durations of 7.2 and 1.8 years, including both trading fees.
projects.decision: The shift modestly lowers sensitivity to a yield rise while giving up gains if yields fall. The fee hurdle makes the size of the intended risk reduction concrete.
projects.falsifier: The interpretation fails if ETF duration, cash availability or the curve differ materially from assumptions. A Fed decision alone cannot identify an underpriced long-bond risk premium.
projects.next: Replace teaching inputs with dated fund analytics and a sourced Treasury curve before execution; model FX hedging separately.
projects.interview: Explain why policy rates and long yields can move differently, and why dollar duration does not include EUR/USD risk.
projects.finding: The pending 2% shift reduces assumed portfolio duration by 0.108 years. Two-leg costs are €12.76; a parallel yield rise of 9.3 bp covers them in the instantaneous approximation.

projects.title: Carry, break-even and funding stress
projects.question: How little adverse currency movement can erase the carry?
projects.method: Calculate financed AUD/JPY and MXN/JPY payoffs with simple deposit/loan interest, 10 bp assumed total cost and September-2024 policy-rate anchors. Derive break-even spot moves and textbook zero-basis forward ratios. Measure historical spot-only tail risk and pair correlation separately.
projects.decision: Two target currencies funded in yen share a common vulnerability. A small quarterly accrual should be compared with a large adverse spot move before allocating capital.
projects.falsifier: Actual forwards, funding spreads, margin calls and collateral remuneration can overturn the indicative return. Without those records, this overlay contributes zero reported portfolio P&L.
projects.next: Archive executable forward points and bid/ask quotes, define collateral and financing, then start a prospective EUR-valued paper ledger.
projects.interview: Distinguish return on borrowed notional from return on margin, covered parity from uncovered expected return, and a spot series from a carry total-return series.
projects.finding: Illustrative quarterly carry is erased by spot losses of 0.92% for AUD/JPY and 2.40% for MXN/JPY. Neither is a funded portfolio trade.

projects.title: CME reverse valuation
projects.question: How much cash-flow growth was embedded in the September-2024 price?
projects.method: Bridge FY2023 operating cash flow to a conservative per-share equity cash proxy, subtracting capex and stock compensation. Model five explicit years and a terminal value, solve implied growth, and show discount-rate/growth and bull/base/bear sensitivities.
projects.decision: An attractive exchange franchise does not guarantee an attractive purchase price. A reverse valuation makes the growth hurdle visible and can challenge an optimistic narrative.
projects.falsifier: A cash proxy that misses recurring reinvestment, financing or competitive pressure is insufficient. A high terminal-value share makes apparently precise fair values especially fragile.
projects.next: Build a current operating forecast from volumes, revenue per contract, product mix, expenses, collateral economics and capital allocation.
projects.interview: Explain why subtract SBC, why there is no extra net-cash add-on here, and why this aged inception model cannot justify a 2026 hold without refreshed inputs.
projects.finding: The September-2024 CME price requires 11.04% annual cash growth under the stated discount assumptions. Base proxy value: $192.35; 77.1% comes from the terminal value.

projects.title: Is more trading actually better?
projects.question: How do buy-and-hold, monthly resets and drift bands compare?
projects.method: Keep the same 16-instrument September-2024 allocation for all three rules. Review at the last calendar weekday and execute at a strictly later common-market close. Charge 25 bp per side and 50 bp for crypto, then vary costs without selecting the best-performing configuration.
projects.decision: Separate allocation maintenance from new investment information. Additional activity should be justified by risk control or improved expected returns, not by making the journal look busy.
projects.falsifier: If a strategy's apparent advantage vanishes with realistic costs, different windows or stable accounting conventions, it is not a robust edge.
projects.next: Register a forward policy before observing returns, extend the dataset, and compare on equal risk rather than maximising the historical headline return.
projects.interview: Explain why a chronological simulation can still suffer from hindsight, why gross turnover counts both legs and why these rules are different from the discretionary historical book.
projects.finding: Buy hold: 26.99% net, €248 fees; Monthly: 27.20% net, €468 fees; Drift: 29.35% net, €394 fees. These are historical comparisons, not verified alpha.

projects.title: Commodity exposure and futures mechanics
projects.question: What risk is owned through gold, silver, copper and oil vehicles?
projects.method: Compare EUR return correlations and volatility of VT, GLD, SLV, CPER and BNO in two windows. Independently illustrate long-futures convergence in backwardation, a flat curve and contango with unchanged spot and explicit collateral/cost assumptions.
projects.decision: Separate physical-metal exposure from futures-based funds. Spot direction alone cannot explain an oil or copper fund's return; diversified-index research does not validate a concentrated commodity bet.
projects.falsifier: Observed diversification can disappear in a new regime. A futures curve, index roll rule or financing convention different from the illustration changes the result.
projects.next: Archive contract-level settlements, expiry schedules, roll rules and collateral yields to decompose actual fund returns.
projects.interview: Explain why contango need not cause an instantaneous cash loss on the roll date, and why neither gold nor silver is a guaranteed short-horizon inflation hedge.
projects.finding: With unchanged spot and an identically resetting 2% contango curve, the illustrative collateralised futures return is -19.69% over twelve months. This is a mechanics example, not a forecast.

projects.title: Novo and Rheinmetall event studies
projects.question: How unusual were the price moves around the thesis-changing releases?
projects.method: Fit a simple EUR market model on sessions -120 through -21 before each release, then measure abnormal returns over -5 through +5. Use VT for the Novo ADR and IEUR for Rheinmetall. Bridge adjusted-price archives at the overlapping date before combining them.
projects.decision: Distinguish a stock-specific repricing from a broad market move. Preserve unfavourable outcomes and connect fundamental releases to a repeatable diagnostic.
projects.falsifier: A different benchmark, concurrent news or non-synchronous prices can materially change abnormal returns. Event selection after the outcome prevents a causal or predictive claim.
projects.next: Pre-register future events and windows, include unaffected controls and sector factors, and separate announcement time from local close time.
projects.interview: Explain alpha and beta estimation, arithmetic CAR versus compounded wealth, event contamination and why three selected events do not establish skill.
projects.finding: NVO 2024-12-20: -18.28% event-day abnormal return; NVO 2025-07-29: -21.59% event-day abnormal return; RHM.DE 2025-03-12: 9.47% event-day abnormal return. Selected events do not establish causality.

projects.title: Cross-asset stress laboratory
projects.question: What breaks when rates, equities, crypto and currencies move together?
projects.method: Apply four explicit, hypothetical joint shocks to the 25 September holdings. Revalue local returns and EUR conversion with their interaction. Approximate IEF and SHY with assumed duration and convexity; reconcile holding-level impacts to total NAV.
projects.decision: Use the largest losses to identify common exposures and specify an acceptable loss budget before considering any hedge.
projects.falsifier: Different FX behaviour, convexity, correlations or liquidity can reverse the scenario ranking. Shock sizes are assumptions, not estimated percentiles.
projects.next: Source dated ETF duration and curve data, add spread and liquidity shocks, and map fund economic currency exposures.
projects.interview: Why can a positive USD move cushion losses for a EUR investor? Which cross term is lost by adding local and currency returns?
projects.finding: The assumed inflation shock produces -17.2% (-21,998 EUR) on the 25 September book. This is a scenario, not a probability or VaR estimate.

projects.title: EUR currency hedge frontier
projects.question: How sensitive is portfolio risk to partial currency hedging and its cost?
projects.method: Compare zero, half, full and estimated minimum-variance hedging of opening USD-listed notional. Estimate the hedge coefficient using observations through 27 September 2024; evaluate later observations with three assumed annual carry drags. Current weights make this a retrospective exposure experiment.
projects.decision: Separate currency protection from expected carry. Compare risk reduction with a cost hurdle before acquiring an actual forward.
projects.falsifier: Quotation currency is not economic exposure. Daily reset assumptions, proxy basis and changing covariance may make a calculated hedge inappropriate.
projects.next: Archive executable EUR/USD forward points and fund look-through before documenting a prospective hedge policy.
projects.interview: Derive Cov(portfolio, hedge-leg)/Var(hedge-leg). Why is hedging every USD-listed ETF potentially an overhedge?
projects.finding: USD-listed positions are 88.5% of NAV. A training-window minimum-variance translation hedge is 98.8% before the 0–100% bound; this is not an economic currency look-through.

projects.title: Factor exposure and model fragility
projects.question: How much of the basket is explained by equity, duration and gold proxies?
projects.method: Regress the fixed current-weight EUR basket on VT, IEF minus SHY, and GLD. Compare pre-inception and recent 252-session windows. Show Newey–West uncertainty, residual volatility, correlation conditioning and first principal-component share.
projects.decision: Identify broad drivers and exposure instability. Large R-squared can be mechanical because regressors are also portfolio holdings.
projects.falsifier: Omitted factors, overlap, collinearity and shifting coefficients undermine interpretation. The intercept is not a risk-free-adjusted alpha estimate.
projects.next: Use non-overlapping, investable factors, explicit EUR cash returns and rolling out-of-sample attribution.
projects.interview: Distinguish statistical fit, investable factor returns and causal explanation; explain why HAC errors do not cure misspecification.
projects.finding: Three tradable proxies explain 92.8% of the fixed-weight basket's daily variation over the last 252 common sessions. Explanatory fit is not causality or alpha.

projects.title: Trend rule with delayed execution
projects.question: Does a transparent long/cash trend rule change the portfolio’s loss profile?
projects.method: Use each instrument’s lagged 252-session EUR return to retain its original weight or move that sleeve to cash. Review monthly and fill only at the next available common close. Compare the same initial allocation without the signal; report all 126/189/252-session and cost sensitivities.
projects.decision: Evaluate drawdown, cash drag, turnover and implementation together. Do not select a parameter because it maximises this short sample’s return.
projects.falsifier: Whipsaws, slow re-entry, stale common dates and hindsight in selecting the universe can erase apparent protection.
projects.next: Preregister one rule and cost assumption, then log forward signals without tuning on the new observations.
projects.interview: Explain the distinction between a past-return signal, its later executable fill, and the published futures momentum literature.
projects.finding: The stated 252-session long/cash rule returned 24.8% after costs versus 27.2% for the same allocation reset monthly. All nine lookback/cost cases are disclosed; none is selected as optimal.

projects.title: Cash-funded volatility targeting
projects.question: What does reducing exposure after volatility rises cost and protect?
projects.method: Estimate 60-session realised EUR basket volatility using only available closes. Scale original risky targets by target-volatility/estimated-volatility, clipped to 25–100%; review monthly and fill later. Compare 8%, 10%, 12% targets and zero/base/double transaction costs.
projects.decision: Treat exposure control as a risk policy with cash drag and turnover. A target is an estimator input, not a guaranteed realised volatility.
projects.falsifier: Gaps can occur before risk is reduced; rapid recoveries can punish delayed re-entry. The policy cannot lever up when the portfolio is below target.
projects.next: Specify a prospective volatility band, review cadence and financing assumptions before comparing realised forward risk.
projects.interview: Why is inverse volatility not inverse variance? Why does no leverage make a low-volatility regime asymmetric?
projects.finding: The 10% target rule realised 10.6% volatility and -11.3% maximum drawdown versus 12.6% and -12.9% for the monthly baseline. A target is not a risk guarantee.

projects.title: Drawdown and recovery anatomy
projects.question: How deep and how long were losses, and how path-dependent is that result?
projects.method: Extract peak–trough–recovery episodes from the reconstructed NAV, including unrecovered episodes. Separately resample the current-weight return proxy into 600 one-year paths at block lengths 1, 5 and 20; retain the full sensitivity rather than selecting a favourable block.
projects.decision: Discuss both capital loss and time underwater. The drawdown tolerated by an investor may differ from a one-day VaR budget.
projects.falsifier: Resampling cannot create unseen crises. Current weights and stationary historical blocks may be poor approximations to future regimes.
projects.next: Extend history across distinct crises and compare explicit liquidity stresses with prospective risk limits.
projects.interview: Why is maximum drawdown not a one-day risk statistic? What information is lost when returns are randomly reordered?
projects.finding: The reconstructed ledger’s deepest drawdown was -12.4%. Its episode lasted 144 recorded sessions; recovery status and dates are retained. Resampling current weights is a separate risk experiment.

projects.title: VaR forecast coverage checks
projects.question: Do simple daily loss forecasts produce the expected number of breaches?
projects.method: Create lagged 250-session historical and exponentially weighted Gaussian risk forecasts at 95% and 99%. Count later exceedances, show Wilson coverage intervals, Kupiec unconditional-coverage likelihood ratios and descriptive adjacent-breach counts.
projects.decision: Check both frequency and clustering before relying on a risk number. A model that passes a small-sample coverage check can still miss crisis losses.
projects.falsifier: The fixed current-weight proxy is hindsight-based. Gaussian tails, sparse 99% exceptions and asymptotic p-values limit inference; clustering is not formally tested here.
projects.next: Maintain a prospective ledger of forecasts and realised hypothetical P&L; add independent clustering and tail-severity tests.
projects.interview: Why does unconditional coverage fail to detect clustered breaches? Explain the zero-exception edge case.
projects.finding: Rolling historical 99% VaR recorded 9 breaches in 484 evaluation sessions (expected 4.8). Coverage and clustering must be examined together.

projects.title: Crypto allocation and correlation stress
projects.question: How much risk can a small Bitcoin/Ether allocation consume?
projects.method: Hold the other current weights fixed and fund 0–5% crypto allocations from EUR cash in the existing BTC/ETH proportion. Show Euler variance shares and an explicitly positive-semidefinite correlation stress. Audit whether weekend price pairs are actually present.
projects.decision: Set crypto exposure by its impact on total portfolio risk and liquidity, not only by its small capital weight.
projects.falsifier: The common-market calendar omits weekend moves; past covariance excludes custody losses and may understate deleveraging.
projects.next: Acquire a complete daily crypto archive and document custody, venue and gap scenarios before increasing the paper allocation.
projects.interview: Explain why capital weight and variance share differ and why an arbitrary shocked correlation matrix may be invalid.
projects.finding: The frozen 2.8% crypto capital allocation contributes 6.4% of sample portfolio variance. Cash-funded alternatives are compared without selecting the best historical return.

projects.title: Protective puts and collar economics
projects.question: What is the actual trade-off between downside protection, premium and foregone upside?
projects.method: Price synthetic three-month European options using Black–Scholes. Compare an unhedged underlying, a 90-strike protective put and a 90/110 collar. Include premium cash opportunity cost and per-leg fees; compare 15%, 25%, 40% assumed volatility.
projects.decision: State the loss floor, upside cap and funding cost explicitly before calling a hedge attractive. These payoffs do not establish that insurance is cheap.
projects.falsifier: Real implied skew, bid/ask costs, dividends, American exercise and basis risk can materially change the trade.
projects.next: Source a dated option chain and contract specifications; write a cash-funded prospective hedge thesis before any paper fill.
projects.interview: Derive put–call parity and explain why P&L divided by underlying notional is not return on option premium.
projects.finding: At 25% assumed volatility, the 90-strike put costs 1.18 per 100 of underlying. The collar exchanges upside above 110 for call premium; neither structure is costless.

projects.title: Prospective thesis and probability register
projects.question: How can future investment judgements become auditable evidence?
projects.method: Validate append-only forecasts and resolutions with timestamped information cutoffs, explicit outcome rules and a SHA-256 chain. Compute binary Brier scores only for resolved registered forecasts. The empty initial register is separate from a synthetic proper-scoring demonstration.
projects.decision: Record probabilities, alternatives and invalidation rules before events. Preserve mistakes and unresolved outcomes; connect any later trade to the original thesis.
projects.falsifier: A rewritten hash chain, selective resolution or vague event definition destroys evidential value. A Git timestamp alone does not verify source availability.
projects.next: Enter the first owner-approved forecast with scripts/record_decision.py and publish its commit before the outcome; retain an external timestamp anchor.
projects.interview: Why does a proper scoring rule encourage honest probabilities, and why is a low score meaningless without a base-rate benchmark?
projects.finding: 0 prospective forecasts and 0 resolved outcomes are registered. No forecasting skill score is claimed. The probability-scoring chart is a labelled mathematical demonstration.

archive.title: Frozen portfolio and Yahoo Finance price archives
archive.application: Accounting inputs and reference closing marks. Retrieved in 2026, not historical point-in-time vintages.

shrink.title: Ledoit & Wolf — Honey, I Shrunk the Sample Covariance Matrix (2003 working paper; 2004 publication)
shrink.application: Structured estimation motivation. The paper cautions against constant correlation across asset classes; both constant-correlation and diagonal targets are sensitivity checks, not validated allocation models. No optimal intensity is estimated.

diversify.title: DeMiguel, Garlappi & Uppal — Optimal versus Naive Diversification (2009)
diversify.application: Estimation error motivates simple benchmark rules; no replication of the paper and no endorsement of these exact weights.

crypto.title: Liu & Tsyvinski — Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency (2018)
crypto.application: Motivates separate crypto risk treatment; an early sample does not establish stable modern correlations.

term.title: Adrian, Crump & Moench — Pricing the Term Structure with Linear Regressions
term.application: Conceptual distinction between expected short rates and term compensation. No ACM model is fitted in this project.

carry.title: Brunnermeier, Nagel & Pedersen — Carry Trades and Currency Crashes (2008)
carry.application: Funding unwind and downside-tail motivation; the project does not reproduce their currency basket study.

basis.title: Borio et al. — Covered Interest Parity Lost (BIS, 2016)
basis.application: Explains why actual forward quotes can differ from frictionless parity; basis is not estimated here.

rates2024.title: September-2024 central-bank rate anchors
rates2024.application: AUD 4.35%, JPY 0.25%, MXN 10.50% are historical policy anchors, not executable matched-maturity lending or borrowing quotes. See docs/SOURCES.md for the BOJ and Banxico releases.

equitycash.title: Damodaran — Free Cash Flow to Equity Discount Models, chapter 14
equitycash.application: Equity cash-flow discounting framework; the CME cash proxy omits a complete financing and operating forecast.

cme2023.title: CME Group FY2023 Form 10-K
cme2023.application: Cash-flow statement: CFO $3,453.8m; property purchases $76.4m; SBC $82.9m. Share denominator is disclosed separately in the input notes.

backtest.title: Bailey et al. — The Probability of Backtest Overfitting (2015)
backtest.application: Motivates reporting all specified rule/cost comparisons rather than presenting only the winner. No PBO statistic is estimated from three rules.

commodities.title: Gorton & Rouwenhorst — Facts and Fantasies about Commodity Futures (2004)
commodities.application: Research on diversified, collateralised futures; not a direct validation of GLD, CPER or BNO.

gold.title: Erb & Harvey — The Golden Dilemma (2013)
gold.application: Cautions against treating gold as a reliable short-horizon inflation hedge.

eventstudy.title: MacKinlay — Event Studies in Economics and Finance (1997)
eventstudy.application: Market-model abnormal-return framework. No significance claim or causal identification is made here.

stress_principles.title: BCBS (2018), Stress testing principles
stress_principles.application: Scenario design and governance motivation. The four assumed shocks are not a regulatory stress test or estimated crisis probabilities.

tsmom.title: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), Time Series Momentum
tsmom.application: Motivates lagged own-return signals. Our monthly long/cash ETF rule is not a replication of the paper’s futures strategy.

volmanaged.title: Moreira & Muir (2016/2017), Volatility-Managed Portfolios
volmanaged.application: Motivates exposure sensitivity to realised volatility. Our capped volatility target differs from the paper’s inverse-variance factor portfolios.

hac.title: Newey & West (1986/1987), A Simple, Positive Semi-Definite, Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent Covariance Matrix
hac.application: OLS coefficient uncertainty uses a Bartlett-weighted HAC estimator with five lags. Approximate intervals do not establish causal exposures.

drawdown.title: Chekhlov, Uryasev & Zabarankin (2005), Drawdown Measure in Portfolio Optimization
drawdown.application: Motivates path-dependent loss analysis. The project measures episodes and block-resampling sensitivity; it does not solve the paper’s optimisation problem.

backtesting.title: Basel Framework MAR32, Backtesting requirements
backtesting.application: Motivates comparison of lagged risk forecasts with subsequent losses. Coverage diagnostics here are educational, not a regulatory backtest or model certification.

blackscholes.title: Black & Scholes (1973), The Pricing of Options and Corporate Liabilities
blackscholes.application: European call/put pricing at assumed constant volatility, with put–call parity tested. No market-implied volatility or tradable quote is inferred.

cboehedges.title: Cboe (2021), Hedging Downside Exposure with PPUT, CLL and CLLZ Indices
cboehedges.application: Institutional context for protective puts and collars. Synthetic strikes and costs do not replicate a Cboe benchmark.

proper_scores.title: Gneiting & Raftery (2007), Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
proper_scores.application: Motivates recording probabilities before outcomes and scoring with binary Brier loss. A theoretical demonstration is kept separate from personal evidence.

disclosure: Built with AI assistance in September–October 2026. Ten studies added on 3 October; portfolio marks remain 25 September and empirical return panels end 18 September. The earlier portfolio is a retrospective reconstruction; these projects were not tools used live in 2024. No demonstrated predictive alpha or real-money track record is claimed.
